mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has been essentially flat-to-declining for four consecutive weeks (-14.0 to -13.9), reflecting persistent consumer caution. Absent a shock, this flat-to-negative momentum will persist, so the next 28-day mean will be equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC values -14.0,-13.3,-13.9,-13.9 show no upward momentum
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC rises by more than 1 point above the last 28-day mean, the momentum-persistence hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has crossed from positive (1.3) to negative (-1.7) over four weeks, indicating a weakening of commuting-linked economic activity. Once WORKPLACES turns negative, associated after-work and lunchtime retail visits drop, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from 1.3 to -1.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the two weeks following WORKPLACES crossing below zero, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT (-9.9 to -11.1) and WORKPLACES (1.3 to -1.7) jointly signal reduced out-of-home circulation; the combined drag is stronger than either series alone because reduced transit use compounds reduced commuting-linked retail stops, producing an amplified decline in RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline week-on-week for 2+ consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show monotonic decline across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite continued joint decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening pandemic restrictions, a rising RESIDENTIAL index (7.3 to 7.9) reflects increased mandated or voluntary at-home time, which directly substitutes for discretionary retail and recreation trips, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from 7.3 to 7.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL continues to climb, this policy-driven substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS decline (-38.0 to -43.1) in mid-August reflects seasonal heat avoidance of outdoor spaces in Hong Kong; this displaced outdoor activity is redirected to air-conditioned indoor retail and recreation venues, producing a modest rise in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped to -43.1 in t-1w, the lowest in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise or falls further while PARKS remains below -40, the seasonal-substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains stable near +10 across all four weeks, indicating essential-goods consumption is unaffected, while RETAIL_REC stays depressed; this divergence signals that consumers are maintaining necessity spending but continuing to avoid discretionary retail, a behavioral pattern expected to persist over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM varies only between 9.6 and 10.4 while RETAIL_REC stays near -14
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC converges toward GROCERY_PHARM's stable positive range within two weeks, the necessity-discretionary divergence hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has steadily worsened each week (-9.9, -10.1, -10.6, -11.1); once TRANSIT falls below -12, reduced accessibility to retail districts via public transport will produce an immediate one-week drop in RETAIL_REC as shoppers forgo trips requiring transit.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has declined every week reaching -11.1 at t-0w, approaching the -12 threshold
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week immediately following TRANSIT crossing below -12, the threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of declining WORKPLACES (1.3 to -1.7) and rising RESIDENTIAL (7.3 to 7.9) indicates a coordinated shift toward remote-work and stay-home policy enforcement; this combination has a compounding suppressive effect on RETAIL_REC beyond either series individually, driving a sustained decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines and RESIDENTIAL rises concurrently for 3+ weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 1.3 to -1.7 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 7.3 to 7.9 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite the continued inverse co-movement of WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
